extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communicators, and anyone pitching stories to journalists
extracted.subtask_short: crafting PR pitches for news coverage
extracted.subtask_description: A concise, journalist-derived checklist of news values to help PR practitioners shape pitches that increase likelihood of media coverage. Focuses on eight concrete criteria journalists use to judge story newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: "How many people are affected by this story? The more, the better."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the scale or reach of the story — national vs. local, number of people affected, potential consequences. Higher-impact events are more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: "When did the news happen? The sooner, the better."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories tied to recent events or breaking developments are prioritized. Pitches should emphasize recency and why the timing matters now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Where is the story located? The closer it is, the more interesting it becomes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local relevance increases interest; tailor pitches to the geographic scope of the target outlet (city, region, nation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: How notable are the key figures involved? A cycling accident becomes newsworthy when the mayor is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name recognition and status of people/organizations in the story raise news value; attach prominent spokespeople or figures where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rarity
rubrics_metrics.description: "How unexpected are the elements of the story?" Standout stories represent unusual or exceptional occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight unusual, exceptional, or surprising aspects that differentiate the story from routine events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this pitch about something we're already covering? Is it part of a trend?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie pitches to ongoing coverage, trending topics, or evolving beats to increase relevance to reporters already tracking the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: "Opposing forces make a story more compelling."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify tensions, disagreements, competition, or stakes that create narrative drive; conflict often hooks audiences and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: "Can you put a face to this story? People care about other people."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use individual stories, characters, or emotional hooks to make abstract issues relatable; include human examples or testimonials when possible.
